reason: Under the Unlimited Mode Pricing heading the page gives $0.05 for T2 and T3, $0.04 for T4g and $0.06 for T8i per vCPU-Hour for Linux, RHEL and SLES, and says the price is the same for all sizes, purchase options and Regions.
The quotes state T8i, T4g, T3a and T3 earn no launch credits and launch as unlimited by default, and that T3 on a Dedicated Host launches as standard with unlimited not supported.
The quote states Capacity Blocks can be reserved for 1 to 182 days and can start within minutes or at a scheduled future date.
The quote states each Capacity Block can have up to 64 instances and up to 256 instances across Capacity Blocks.
The quote states that unlike On-Demand Capacity Reservations, Capacity Block pricing cannot be combined with Savings Plans or Reserved Instance discounts.
The quotes state the price depends on supply and demand at purchase, is charged up front when the reservation is made, and does not change after reservation.

The quote states that by default reservations automatically match new and running instances with matching type, platform, AZ and tenancy, and that you can instead target a reservation; the context adds that targeting controls which instances run in it.
The quotes state per-second billing with a 60-second minimum and that billing starts as soon as the reservation is provisioned in the account.

The table rows under the Minimum cancellation rate header give no charge at 8 or more weeks, 25% of total at 2 to 8 weeks, 50% of total within 2 weeks, and 50% of remaining after delivery; the claim keeps the minimum wording.
The quote states reservations are charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate whether used or not, a matching instance pays nothing for the reservation, and there are no upfront or additional charges.
The quotes state Savings Plans and Regional RI discounts apply to reservations with matching attributes and zonal RI discounts do not apply.

The quotes state you specify the date and commitment, billing starts at the future date, you can't decrease count or duration during the commitment, and after it you can modify or cancel without charge.
The FAQ quote states reservations can be for immediate use or delivered between 5 and 120 days in the future.
The quote states future-dated reservations need an instance count with a minimum of 32 vCPUs, for example at least 8 m5.xlarge; the family condition is in the next line of the Limitations list.
The quotes state cancellation is free when active with no or an elapsed commitment, and running instances continue at On-Demand rates or a matching Savings Plans or Regional RI rate.
The quotes state reservations are in a specific AZ for any duration, and an immediate-use reservation has no term commitment and can be modified or cancelled at any time.
The quote is the claim word for word.
The quote states reservations can't be used with Dedicated Hosts and can be used with Dedicated Instances.
The quote states reservations are not transferable between accounts but can be shared with other accounts.
The quote states reservations can be created in cluster placement groups and spread and partition groups are not supported.
The quote states Capacity Reservations count toward On-Demand Instance quotas even if unused; the context gives the per-account per-Region scope.
The quote states the Graviton migration improved performance and let Logz.io reduce infrastructure costs by up to 30 percent, double what it expected.
The quote is future tense ('JPL will also use' On-Demand and ODCR for critical processing); the claim states it as current practice ('uses'). Rewording to 'plans to use' or 'will use' would match.
The quote is future tense ('JPL will take advantage of Spot Instances for scaling'); the claim states it as current practice ('uses'). The reason, fault tolerance, is supported.
The quote states SmartNews lowered compute costs for its ML workloads by 15 percent using AWS Graviton.
The quote states SmartNews scales capacity up and down and uses an internal monitoring system with best practices such as a price-capacity optimized allocation strategy.
The quote states Spot Instances cut costs for the main compute workload by up to 50 percent.
The document history row dated December 1, 2024 states you can now control discovery and use of AMIs by specifying criteria AMIs must meet.
The FAQ quotes state AL2 reached end of support on 2026-06-30, no longer receives standard security updates, customers should migrate to AL2023, and AL2023 is supported until June 2029.
The document history row dated October 20, 2023 states block public access for AMIs is now enabled by default for new accounts and existing accounts with no public AMIs.
The What's New post dated Sep 4, 2026 states owners can specify supported or unsupported types, non-permitted launches are blocked, and by default an AMI can launch on any type.
The post dated Aug 10, 2026 states EC2 sends HTTP or HTTPS requests to the chosen port and path, reports status every 60 seconds, and Auto Scaling groups replace instances that report unhealthy.
The document history row dated November 21, 2024 states Capacity Blocks for ML can now be reserved for up to 6 months (182 days).
Two document history rows dated November 21, 2024 state Capacity Blocks can start as soon as 30 minutes and existing Capacity Blocks can be extended.
Document history rows give sharing within the organization on February 2, 2026 and Local Zones on February 25, 2026; the Considerations list states UltraServer Capacity Blocks can't be shared.
The document history row dated November 20, 2024 states instances can now be set to run only in a Capacity Reservation or resource group.
The document history row dated October 31, 2022 states Elastic IP addresses can now be transferred between AWS accounts.
The document history row dated November 21, 2024 states you can now request Capacity Reservations for a future date.

The evidence gives two dates: the document history row says June 2, 2026, but the cited What's New post for the same launch is posted Jun 10, 2026; I cannot tell which date the feature became available, so the claim 'On 2026-06-02 Amazon EC2 made it possible' is not certain. The cancel-with-possible-charge content is supported.
The post dated Sep 28, 2026 states you can now postpone the start date before delivery and the commitment duration can increase depending on when you postpone.
